-(1) The area of the auditorium shall be not less than 3 Auditorium. square feet to each person to be admitted.

(2) All floors and balconies shall be constructed in rein­ forced concrete or other approved materials.

(3) The height between auditorium floor and ceiling shall be not less than 12 feet between balcony and ceiling not less than 10 feet.

(4) There shall be provided:- A. A clear passage or gangway not less than 4 feet wide around the auditorium. B. Gangways not less than 4 feet wide running parallel to the seating in such position as the Board may decide.

(5) No obstruction shall be allowed in any stairway or gang­ way and no standing or sitting by members of the public shall be permitted in any stairway or alley way.

(6) Should steps occur in any gangway they shall be suitably illuminated during all preforrnances.

-(1) Seats shall be ganged together in a row of not less Seating. than five, or each seat shall be securely fastened to the floor.

(2) No seat is to be more than seven seats from a gangway, counted in the line of seating.

(3) No barricades whatever shall be erected round indivi­ dual seats or blocks of seats.

(4) When all seating space in the body of the hall or in the galleries is occupied, all booking shall cease and a notice shall be exhibited outside the entrance notifying that part or the whole of the theatre is full.

(2) There shall be provided:- A. One foot of urinal space for every 100 seats or' one urinal stall for every 200 seats. B. One male closet for every 200 seats. C. One female closet for every 100 seats,

(3) The building is to be closed twice a year for such clea­ nsing, disinfecting, lime-washing; painting and repair work as may be considered necessary by the Board. Right of 11.-(1) Free access is to be given at all times for inspection Access. by the Board or their authorised agent.

(2) No person shall enter the building between performances except on-business. Lighting. 12.-(1) No naked lights or fires are to be used in the building except with the specific approval of the Board in writing.

(2) The building shall be fitted with secondary lighting of a type approved by the Board. Projection 13.-(1) Cinematograph projection apparatus is to be fixed Room. in an enclosure or room built of fire resisting material of suitable size to allow operators to work freely and the materials, construc­ tion and size must be to the approval of the Board.

(2) This enclosure or room must be outside the auditorium if possible and fitted with a self closing fireproof door opening outwards, preferably onto an open space or landing fitted with railings where necessary.

(3) This door must net be locked whilst the projection en­ closure is occupied.

(4) All openings in front of the enclosure into the auditorium are to be glazed and these must not be more than two to each projection machine with a total area of not more than 1-!. square feet.

(5) Each opening is to be fitted with a self closing metal shutter so arranged that they can be operated for closure by a release mechanism worked from the position of each projection machine and also from outside the door of the projection room.

(6) Where possible there shall be no other opening, door or connection to the auditorium except the above mentioned projec­ tion openings.

(7) Each projection machine shall have fitted above it a metal hood and vent opening into the open air outside the building. Rewind 14.---(1) The rewinding, pointing and piecing of films shall Room. not be carried out in the projection room but in a separate fire­ proof enclosure fitted with a door as for the projection room.

(2) The table in this rewind room is to be surfaced with non­ ferrous metal (e.g. lead).

(3) No smoke or fumes are to be allowed to escape from either room into the auditorium. Film 15.-(1) No film except such as are necessary for the imme­ diate. Storage. performance are to be stored in either the projection or rewind rooms.

(2) Films may only be stcred in metal cases in a film storage vault, constructed of approved fire-proof material and situated out­ side and, where, possible, distinct from, the main or other building.

(3) This vault it to be fitted with a self closing fire-proof door and must be adequately ventilated.

(4) No naked lights are allowed in this vault.

(5) No unauthorised shall be allowed in the pro­ person jection, rewind or film rooms or on the or in the storage stage dressing rooms.

Permit for 25. No building shall be used as a theatre without a permit Theatre. to this effect being' issued by the Board. This permit shall be prominently displayed within the main entrance to the building, and shall state the time during which it is valid, and shall be in the form shown in Appendix "B" hereto. Fees. 26.-(1) Fees payable for a permit to use a building as a theatre shall be as follows:- Number of seats. Fee per day. Fee per mensem. Not more than 200 $ 1.-$10.- Not more than 500 $ 2.-$20.- Not more than 1000 s 5.--$25.-- Above 1000 $10.--$50.--

(2) The permit fees may be reduced or waived by the Board where the use as a theatre is for a limited time or where the show is for charitable purposes or where no admission charges are made.

(3) Fees payable for the issue of a licence for performance shall be as follows:-- Cinematograph $3.-$100.- Combined cinematograph and theatre performance $3.-s 75.- All other performances $3.-$ 50.-

(4) The licence fees may be reduced or waived at the dis­ cretion of the Board, for shows where no fee is charged for admis­ sion or shows for charitable purposes. Penalty. 27.-(1) The holder of a licence or permit who allows any contravention of these By-laws by any member of his staff or other person, shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $500.

(2) Any other person contravening any of these By-laws shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $100. I. O. GILBERT, British Resident, Brunei. APPENDIX "A".
